newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKISH GSM COMPANY IN $570-MLN SYNDICATION DEAL.
newsitem.headline: TURKISH GSM COMPANY IN $570-MLN SYNDICATION DEAL.

text.p: Turkish cellular phone company Turkcell is planning a $570 million syndication loan to be used in its payment for licences of its Global System of Mobiles (GSM) network and some other investments, bankers said.

They said $500 million of the loan would be used for payments to Turk Telekom, which has contracted the country's GSM operation to two companies, Turkcell and Telsim, which have not paid for the licences yet.
Turk Telekom, the state-run telecommunications company, demands $500 million from each of the two companies this year or will scrap the contract.
Banker said Turkcell, a joint venture between a local firm and the Swedish Ericsson, was working to choose a lead manager for the syndication from among five or six banks.
Some bankers said the arrangers could be Bankers Trust, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and JP Morgan.
